summary: Roland Harweg was a linguist who studied under Peter Hartmann and Alfred Schmitt. He held posts at the University of Münster (circa 1963–1969) and Ruhr University Bochum (circa 1969–1999).
Roland Knyvet Wilson was an Indologist who earned his B.A. at the University of Cambridge (circa 1859–1863). He later served at Cambridge as Reader in Indian Law from 1884 to 1893.

Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990). He has held positions at the University of Marburg, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Bologna.

Historian Roland Wenzlhuemer studied at the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held posts at the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient, Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Basel, Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich.

A scholar of Tibetology and Sinology, Rolf Alfred Stein studied at several institutions, including the University of Paris. His career included posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, INALCO, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

Rolf Hiersche, a linguist and Indologist, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle. He held posts at Humboldt University, Free University of Berlin, the University of Lille, and the University of Giessen.

Rolf Scheuermann works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Helmut Tauscher, he earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna and held posts at Vienna, Leipzig, the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich.
Rolf-Heinrich Koch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who held posts attested at Kyoto University in 1997 and the University of Oslo in 1998.

Working in religious studies and philosophy, Romain Rolland was educated at institutions including the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris. He held positions at Lycée Henri-IV, ENS, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Paris.

Archaeologist and Iranian studies scholar Roman Ghirshman studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Louvre. He held positions at the Musée du Louvre, Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan, Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale, and Aix-Marseille University.

Linguist Roman Jakobson studied at Moscow University under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and at the German University of Prague. He held academic posts at Masaryk University, Harvard University, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and completed her doctorate under A. L. Basham at SOAS. She held posts at Kurukshetra University, Delhi University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry is an active scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer, active in Buddhist studies, studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 as well as under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology who held posts as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and as Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser, working in religious studies and philosophy, studied under Koshin Ogui. He has held academic posts at Loyola University Chicago (circa 1992–1997) and San Francisco State University (circa 1997).
Sinologist Ronald Egan earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University. He held positions at Harvard, Wellesley College, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Stanford University.

Ronald Eric Emmerick, a scholar of Iranian, Indological, and Tibetan studies, was educated at Sydney, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held appointments at St John's College, the University of Chicago, SOAS, and the University of Hamburg.
Ronald Herman Poelmeijer was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied at the University of Amsterdam and served as Lecturer of Tibetan at Leiden University.

Ronald Inden is a scholar of Indology and history who held an appointment at the University of Chicago, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.
